item.title: Signing data structures the wrong way
item.description:
📝 If a node in this system signs a TreeRoot and injects the signature into the network, an attacker might try to forge a KeyRevoke message that serializes byte-for-byte into the same message as the signed tree root, then staple the TreeRoot signature onto the KeyRevoke data structure. A verifier might be fooled into “verifying” a statement that the signer never intended. Developers should use simple tooling, either in the IDE or CLI, to generate these random domain separators and insert them into their protocol specifications.
🔗 Read more: https://blog.foks.pub/posts/domain-separation-in-idl/
